arxiv-2303-10061.title: The nonlocal advection diffusion equation and the two-slit experiment in quantum mechanics
arxiv-2303-10061.creator: Glenn Webb
arxiv-2303-10061.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Glenn Webb. A partial differential equation model is analyzed for the two-slit experiment of quantum mechanics. The state variable of the equation is the probability density function of particle positions. The equation has a diffusion term corresponding to the random movement of particles, and a nonlocal advection term corresponding to the movement of particles in the transverse direction perpendicular to their forward movement. The model is compared to the Schrödinger equation model of the experiment. The model supports the ensemble interpretation of quantum mechanics.

arxiv-2305-09797.description: Abstract We give a fully analytical description of radial and angular geodesics for massive particles that travel in the spacetime provided by a ( 3 + 1 ) (3+1) -dimensional scale-dependent black hole in the cosmological background, for which, the quantum corrections are assumed to be small.

arxiv-2402-11709.title: GNNavi : Navigating the Information Flow in Large Language Models by Graph Neural Network
arxiv-2402-11709.creator: Shuzhou Yuan, Ercong Nie, Michael Färber, Helmut Schmid, Hinrich Schütze
arxiv-2402-11709.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit strong In-Context Learning (ICL) capabilities when prompts with demonstrations are used. However, fine-tuning still remains crucial to further enhance their adaptability. Prompt-based fine-tuning proves to be an effective fine-tuning method in low-data scenarios, but high demands on computing resources limit its practicality. We address this issue by introducing a prompt-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approach.

arxiv-2412-19188.title: New Physics in the 3-3-1 models

arxiv-2412-19188.description: Abstract Two main ingredients of current particle physics such as local gauge symmetry and mass generation via the Higgs mechanism being basic ground of the Standard Model are widely confirmed by experimental data. However, some problems such as neutrino masses, dark matter, baryon asymmetry of Universe have clearly indicated that the Standard Model cannot be the ultimate theory of nature.

pmc-10691385.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). PurposeStudies showing problematic sleep patterns in blind and visually impaired children are often based on (parent) self-report. The purpose was to compare sleep patterns of blind children to normally sighted peers using objective measures.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, 100 blind (best-corrected visual acuity <3/60) and 100 age- and gender-matched normally sighted children aged 7 to 17 years wore a digital activity monitoring device for 1 week.

pmc-11343380.creator: Olga Perski, Dimitra Kale, Corinna Leppin, Tosan Okpako, David Simons, Stephanie P. Goldstein, Eric Hekler, Jamie Brown, Calvin Or, Calvin Or, Calvin Or, Calvin Or
pmc-11343380.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Specific moments of lapse among smokers attempting to quit often lead to full relapse, which highlights a need for interventions that target lapses before they might occur, such as just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs). To inform the decision points and tailoring variables of a lapse prevention JITAI, we trained and tested supervised machine learning algorithms that use Ecological Momentary Assessments (EMAs) and wearable sensor data of potential lapse triggers and lapse incidence.

pmc-11544376.description: BackgroundMeckel's diverticulum, a congenital anomaly arising from incomplete obliteration of the omphalomesenteric duct, often remains asymptomatic but can lead to complications such as diverticulitis and perforation.
